The Alaska Railroad’s Denali Star train runs between Anchorage and Fairbanks, taking 12 hours to cover the 350-mile trip. The train runs once daily in either direction during the summer months; at the half-way point—south of the Denali Park station—the two trains meet and stop to transfer some of the staff.

The enchanting image of the courting birds taking part in their traditional mating ritual was taken by engineer Paul Biggs, 51, at Waverley Lakes in Orgreave, South Yorks. Dad-of-three Paul, who lives in Sheffield, said: The photo makes me smile at the tenderness and love  it is a pair of swans very much in love.SEE MERCURY COPY
